messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — I ran a focused throughput bench for the new q8 onboarding of `rw-small` across H100/A100 in us-east / us-west / eu-west. Pasting compact numbers + notes.

Maya: ```
H100 us-east  -> p50 28ms  p95 110ms  throughput 420 qps
H100 us-west  -> p50 30ms  p95 140ms  throughput 410 qps
H100 eu-west  -> p50 34ms  p95 210ms  throughput 350 qps

A100 us-east  -> p50 45ms  p95 220ms  throughput 300 qps
A100 us-west  -> p50 48ms  p95 260ms  throughput 280 qps
A100 eu-west  -> p50 52ms  p95 410ms  throughput 200 qps
```

Alex: eu-west p95 on A100 is wild — >400ms. Did routing change or an extra hop appear? :eyes:

Maya: I pulled traces for a couple slow requests. eu-west flows for a subset (~12%) are traversing `edge-proxy-3` -> `egress-nat-2` due to an emergency failover rule we had last week. Trace sample: https://redwood.internal/trace/0a1b2c (see span graph).

Priya: Kernel selector was identical across regions? which attention kernel for q8 path?

Maya: On H100 we take `fused_attn` (fast path). On A100 the q8 codegen currently falls back to `gemm-optimized` kernels for quant path (we're still onboarding optimized q8 kernels for A100). That plus the extra hop explains the big tail.

Sam: Did you see the warmup curve? Could be cold-KV/cache miss amplification on tails.

Maya: Warmup excluded (ran 2k warm requests first). p95 spike persists post-warm. Network hop + slower kernel seems like the main cause.

Ryan: Suggest a 10% routing canary preferring local-pop shortest path for eu-west to test impact. Also try forcing fused_attn on A100 as an experiment.

Maya: Kicking both now. Commands I'm using:
```
# routing canary 10% to prefer-local in eu-west
redwoodctl routing update --service rw-small --policy prefer-local --region eu-west --canary 10%
# force kernel override on canary hosts (for A100)
redwoodctl runtime set --model rw-small --kernel fused_attn --target-pool a100-eu-canary
```

deploy-bot: canary rollout started (10%) for rw-small in eu-west @ 1715236160

Maya: Re-ran bench after canary stabilized (1k requests). New condensed numbers:
```
H100 eu-west  -> p50 33ms  p95 180ms  throughput 370 qps
A100 eu-west  -> p50 50ms  p95 230ms  throughput 240 qps  (forced fused_attn)
```

Alex: Nice — p95 on H100 improved ~30ms, and A100 down from 410ms -> 230ms with kernel override + routing canary.

Priya: Note: I ran a quick eval on the regression set for the same time window — q8 hallucation rate nudged up by ~0.8% in eu-west during the initial failover tail. Flagging as a quality signal.

Maya: Opened INF-4982 with perf traces, canary configs, and eval artifacts. Link: https://redwood.issue/INF-4982 :point_up:

Ryan: Actionable ops items: 1) remove emergency egress failover for eu-west (prefer local egress), 2) promote A100 q8 kernel optimizations to stable pool, 3) reserve +30% headroom for eu-west A100 until kernel path stabilized. I'll file infra change with ETA ~4h.

Sam: For capacity sizing: based on throughputs above, assume 200 qps per A100 in eu-west for stable buffers -> plan slots accordingly. If you prefer conservative, size for 150 qps during rollout.

Maya: Thanks. I'll run a longer 10k req soak on the canary and share full plots (latency CDFs + p50/p95 over time). Uploading charts to: https://redwood.infra/bench/1715236042/plots.zip

Alex: Good plan. After soak and validation from Priya on regression evals, let's schedule a staged promote. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Priya: I'll re-run eval suite post-soak and comment on INF-4982 with exact delta table.

Ryan: I'll also coordinate edge-proxy config change with networking (low risk). ETA 4h.

Maya: TL;DR: eu-west tail was combo of extra hop + suboptimal A100 q8 kernel. Canary routing + kernel override dropped p95 ~45% on affected hosts. Follow-ups: infra ticket (INF-4982), promote kernels, reserve capacity.

Alex: ack. Short and actionable.
